definition: the highest point; ideal or culminating example
memoryTip: Apo-theos: raised to godlike status—the peak or ideal.
correctPassage: The performance was widely seen as the apotheosis of her career.
wrongPassages: Critics called the unfinished draft the apotheosis of her earliest, weakest work.
The apotheosis of the project was the first rough sketch before any research began.
After the scandal, the film became the apotheosis of everything the studio wanted to forget.

definition: describing a work of visual art in literary form
memoryTip: Ekphrasis = words that re-paint art—a poem about a painting.
correctPassage: Her ekphrastic poem traces each brushstroke of the museum's new landscape.
wrongPassages: His ekphrastic novel never mentioned any painting, sculpture, or photograph.
The lab report was ekphrastic, listing only measurements with no visual subject.
She filed an ekphrastic budget memo that ignored every image in the catalog.

definition: relating to an agent or the capacity to act
memoryTip: Agent-ial: about who can act—having agency.
correctPassage: The theory emphasizes the agential capacity of communities, not only institutions.
wrongPassages: The agential statue sat motionless while visitors walked past it for hours.
Critics called the plot agential because no character ever made a choice.
The agential sample under the microscope showed no motion and no living cells.

definition: the state of being annoyed or worried
correctPassage: Minor technical glitches were a constant source of vexation.
wrongPassages: Her only vexation was the calm joy she felt finishing the puzzle early.
The award speech filled him with pure vexation and lifelong contentment.
Guests described the party as a vexation of laughter, ease, and warm welcome.

definition: words that imitate the sound they name
memoryTip: Buzz, hiss, boom—words that sound like what they mean.
correctPassage: In the comic, every crash panel was filled with bold onomatopoeia.
wrongPassages: The abstract essay relied on onomatopoeia without any sound-imitating words at all.
Her onomatopoeia chapter discussed only silent geometric shapes and color theory.
He labeled pure math symbols as onomatopoeia even though they name no sound.

definition: not honorable in character or purpose
memoryTip: Ig-noble: not noble—base or dishonorable motives.
correctPassage: Betraying a colleague for promotion was an ignoble act.
wrongPassages: Rescuing strangers at great personal risk was widely praised as ignoble.
The scholarship fund was an ignoble effort to help students who could not pay.
Historians called her lifelong public service an ignoble model for future leaders.

memoryTip: Purloin = quietly pocket something that isn't yours.
correctPassage: Someone had managed to purloin several rare maps from the archive.
wrongPassages: She offered to purloin the gift by wrapping it carefully and handing it over in person.
The museum will purloin the painting by returning it to the original owner.
He planned to purloin the missing funds by transferring them back into the account.

correctPassage: The theft was brazen: it happened in full view of security cameras.
wrongPassages: His brazen apology was whispered in private and full of genuine shame.
She made a brazen request only after hiding for weeks and avoiding every camera.
The brazen clerk blushed, stammered, and quietly withdrew the complaint.

memoryTip: Venal for sale—open to bribes and corruption.
correctPassage: A venal official accepted bribes to overlook safety violations.
wrongPassages: The venal judge returned every gift and recused herself from the case.
Voters trusted his venal record of refusing all donations from lobbyists.
Her venal ethics code barred any employee from accepting money or favors.

definition: a surface reused after earlier writing was erased; layered history
memoryTip: Scraped parchment rewritten—old layers still show through.
correctPassage: The city is a palimpsest of architectural styles from many centuries.
wrongPassages: The brand-new blank notebook was a pure palimpsest with no prior marks at all.
He called the single-use form a palimpsest because it could never be written on twice.
The palimpsest wall was poured yesterday and has never held another design.
